finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts::multi-statement detection strips string literals with a naive regex whose quote pairing differs from postgres (e'' escapes, dollar quoting), so statement stacking may be possible
evidence: sql-validator.ts:~58-60 strips literals with /'[^']*'/g and then splits on ';', while datasource.service.ts executes the ORIGINAL dto.query via client.query(text) (simple-query protocol, multi-statement capable). The regex's quote phasing genuinely diverges from Postgres for E-strings: in E'\'' pg consumes three quotes and ends outside a string, whereas the regex pairs the first two and is left mis-phased, so the next quote opens a pseudo-string that swallows subsequent ';' characters. A payload such as `SELECT E'\'' AS x) AS y; SET ROLE nobody; SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'z'` passes the first-token check, the keyword blacklist (SET/COPY/DO/CALL are absent), and the collapsed single-statement check, yet parses as three balanced statements once wrapped in `SELECT * FROM (...) AS _q LIMIT 10001`. Caveats: I reasoned the payload rather than running it against a live server, and sql-validator.ts is pre-existing code untouched by this diff (the controller gates on workspace membership, so the escalation is member-to-member on a shared datasource).
